title: Hallow's End
content: Hallow's End runs each year from October 18 to October 31, decorating capital cities with pumpkins and candy buckets in inns for trick-or-treating. Its centerpiece is the Headless Horseman, who appears in Scarlet Monastery's graveyard and can be queued for through the Dungeon Finder. He drops one of three epic rings (Ring of Ghoulish Glee, The Horseman's Seal or Wicked Witch's Band) and Weighted Jack-o'-Lanterns, and the run rewards a Loot-Filled Pumpkin that can hold the Magic Broom, the Flying Broom or, rarely, The Horseman's Reins mount.

title: Feast of Winter Veil
content: The Feast of Winter Veil is WoW's Christmas-themed holiday, running from December 15 through January 2. Players collect a daily gift from under the tree beside Greatfather Winter in Ironforge or Orgrimmar, buy toys and treats from the traveling Smokywood Pastures vendor, and can start snowball fights or use a Handful of Snowflakes to turn friends into reindeer. There is no dedicated Winter Veil mount, but achievements like Merrymaker (completing every holiday task) award a title, and the classic 'Metzen the Reindeer' summon is a well-known joke item tied to the season.

title: Brewfest
content: Brewfest runs from September 20 to October 4 at fairgrounds outside Ironforge and Orgrimmar, where players ram-race, sample brews from the Brewfest quartermaster for tokens, and fight the drunken boss Coren Direbrew inside Blackrock Depths (also queueable through the Dungeon Finder). Defeating Direbrew drops a loot bag with a chance at the Great Brewfest Kodo or the Swift Brewfest Ram mount, making his fight the event's main draw for collectors. Brewfest carries no reputation of its own; the daily quests and the ram race pay Brewfest Prize Tokens, spent with a Token Redeemer on holiday-only gear, steins, and trinkets.

title: Midsummer Fire Festival
content: The Midsummer Fire Festival burns from June 21 to July 4 around bonfires placed in most major cities and zones. Players tend their own faction's flame, try to douse the rival faction's fire and relight their own from it, and dance around the Ribbon Pole for a festive buff; visiting every bonfire and completing the fire-themed dailies works toward the Fire Festival meta-achievement and title. Rewards are mostly cosmetic -- torch-tossing toys and a Brazier of Dancing Flames trinket -- with no dedicated mount tied to the holiday.

title: Lunar Festival
content: Lunar Festival runs from February 1 to February 14 and centers on visiting Elders scattered across nearly every zone on both continents, each granting the Elders' Blessing buff and a bit of Lunar Festival lore. Players also toss coins into the fountain at Moonglade for a random small reward, and can take on Omen, an enormous spectral beast that spawns as a group-killable target in Moonglade for the duration of the event. Collecting blessings from enough Elders unlocks the elder title and a fireworks-launching trinket.

title: Love is in the Air
content: Love is in the Air runs from February 10 to February 23; Wrath of the Lich King's patch 3.3 expanded it from a minor vanilla holiday into a full event centered on a farcical boss fight against Apothecary Hummel and his two partners in Shadowfang Keep, queued through the Dungeon Finder. Defeating Hummel drops a loot bag with a small chance at the Big Love Rocket, one of the game's most sought-after rare mounts. Players also collect Lovely Charms from monsters everywhere to trade for perfume, cologne, and the companion pet Peddlefeet, and can propose to friends with a Silver Bell or invite them to disco-dance atop a caged Love Fool.

title: Children's Week
content: Children's Week runs from April 30 to May 6. Players adopt a war orphan from the Orphan Matron in their faction's capital and escort it on a tour of iconic locations, including a Northrend leg added for Wrath of the Lich King that has players take their orphan through Icecrown or Borean Tundra. It is also when the School of Hard Knocks achievement is available, which sends players into the battlegrounds with the orphan following them to capture a flag, assault a tower, and the like -- a notoriously unpopular week for battleground regulars. Completing the full questline awards a faction-specific orphan companion pet.

title: Pilgrim's Bounty
content: Pilgrim's Bounty is WoW's Thanksgiving-themed holiday, added with Wrath of the Lich King and running from November 21 to November 27 at a feast table set up outside every major city. Players cook and serve dishes like Cranberry Chutney, Pumpkin Pie, and Slow-Roasted Turkey to seated guests of both factions for reputation and Pilgrim's Bounty Buckets, and can earn the Pilgrim's Paunch food-coma buff for overeating. The Turkinator achievement, earned by killing wild turkeys that spawn worldwide during the event, rounds out the holiday's meta-achievement.

title: Darkmoon Faire
content: The Darkmoon Faire is a travelling carnival with games, vendors and the fortune teller Sayge. It sets up for about a week in Elwynn Forest, Mulgore or Terokkar Forest, and each of those three places gets it once every three months. Silas Darkmoon is there, Selina Dourman gives information, Gelvas Grimegate redeems Darkmoon Faire Prize Tickets, and Lhara and Professor Thaddeus Paleo sell exotic goods and cards.

title: Argent Tournament
content: The Argent Tournament is the Argent Crusade's jousting hub in Icecrown, with daily quests from level 77. Dailies pay Champion's Seals, which each faction's quartermaster there takes: 100 seals buy the city's racial mount (Stormwind Steed, Ironforge Ram, Gnomeregan Mechanostrider, Exodar Elekk, Darnassian Nightsaber, Orgrimmar Wolf, Thunder Bluff Kodo, Silvermoon Hawkstrider, Darkspear Raptor or Forsaken Warhorse) and 150 buy the Argent Hippogryph mount.
